canonical.title: Find single element in sorted array

narrative.title: The Unpaired Beacon in a Twinned Sensor Row
narrative.scenario: A sensor row registers readings in sorted order where every model appears exactly twice - once for the primary unit and once for its standby - except one model whose standby was never commissioned. The maintenance query must find that lone model using only logarithmic probes over the sorted row.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers, sorted in non-decreasing order, where exactly one value appears once and every other value appears exactly twice.
narrative.outputFormat: The value that appears exactly once.
constraints: An O(log n) algorithm with O(1) space is required

testCases.explanation: Every pairing survives until the lone 2, which breaks the alternating twos pattern.
The pairing pattern stays intact left of 10 and collapses right of it, isolating the unpaired beacon.

hintLevels: Level 1: Before the lone value appears, the first copy of every pair sits at an even index; after it, that alignment flips.
Level 2: Probe and check the parity of the index: an even index matching its right neighbour means the anomaly is further right, otherwise it is at or left of the probe.
Level 3: Converge until the bounds meet so the anomaly index is isolated, and a one-element row must return its only value without reading past the end.
